newsitem.title: CHILE: Analysts waiting to see on Santa Isabel.
newsitem.headline: Analysts waiting to see on Santa Isabel.

text.p: Investors reacted positively to the decision by the founder of Chilean supermarket chain Santa Isabel to sell his shareholding, although it is too soon to judge the impact of the deal, said retail analysts.
The company announced Thursday that Eduardo Elberg planned to sell his 37 percent stake in the company for $230 million to The Velox Group which controls Argentine supermarket chain Disco SA.
"It's too early to jump to the conclusion that it is dramatically good or bad news," said one analyst who declined to be named.
"At least it eliminates ongoing concerns about what would happen to Mr Elberg's shares and the people who have acquired the interest are dedicated to the industry."

Santa Isabel's American Depositary Receipts climbed 4.06 percent on Wall Street to 25-5/8 midsession Thursday on news of the sale. The company's shares climbed 3.6 percent at the opening to 725 pesos before falling back to 710 pesos in afternoon trade.

Under the outline deal, Santa Isabel and Disco will continue to operate as completely separate companies although they may sign a deal to share industry knowledge. The final terms of the pact are expected to be agreed within the next 10 days.
"For Santa Isabel, the most important thing is Disco's experience in the highly competitive Argentine market," said Jorge Holzer, an analyst at Larrain Vial.
"They could pass their know-how onto Santa Isabel which is expanding in the region."
Santa Isabel, Chile's largest supermarket chain, already operates stores in Peru and Paraguay and has plans to move into Ecuador."
The link with Buenos Aires-based Disco could also give Santa Isabel access on more favourable terms to Argentine suppliers, said Holzer.

But some investors are concerned that the deal does not signify any advance in Santa Isabel's plans to form a strategic alliance with an international firm to set up hypermarkets, said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investments.
